algorithm: The algorithm implements a hybrid inventory control policy: a constant-order startup phase that gradually transitions into a feedback control law. It targets (i) a safety on-hand buffer, (ii) a desired total pipeline level proportional to lead time L and a baseline order size, and (iii) smoothness by stabilizing the newest pipeline slot. A deadband suppresses small fluctuations, and the order is capped for safety.

The algorithm implements a pipeline-aware base-order policy with gradual feedback activation. It starts from a baseline constant order 'base_order', then (as the pipeline fills) applies proportional feedback to steer (i) near-term available inventory (on-hand plus imminent arrival) toward a target buffer, (ii) total pipeline toward L*base_order, and (iii) the newest pipeline slot toward base_order for smoothing. Orders are clamped to be nonnegative and capped by 'order_cap'.

The algorithm implements a pipeline-filling inventory policy with risk-sensitive feedback. It begins with a baseline constant order 'base_order' and gradually activates feedback as the pipeline becomes sufficiently filled. The feedback corrects (i) immediate availability (on-hand plus the next arriving pipeline slot) toward a target buffer, (ii) total pipeline toward L*base_order, and (iii) near-term pipeline mass (first 1–2 slots) toward a local target to avoid starving early arrivals. In addition, it applies a nonlinear emergency boost when immediate availability falls below the safety buffer, using a power law (shortfall^gamma) to respond more aggressively to critical shortages. Orders are clamped to be nonnegative and capped by 'order_cap'.
